verdict.theme: Flexible workspace and managed offices
verdict.rationale: Awfis leases and operates coworking and managed offices, a real-estate services business riding GCC and AI-driven office demand rather than a forward-looking industry itself. Management reported FY26 operating EBITDA up 37% with margins expanding ~350bps to 36.8%, PAT before exceptionals up 66%, a INR130 crore design-and-build order book already won, and guided to 25-27% FY27 revenue growth on better per-seat realizations.
verdict.quote: Premiumization is translating into structurally better realization, stronger pricing power, longer client tenures

verdict.theme: Quick-service restaurants, McDonald's India franchise
verdict.rationale: Management describes a conventional QSR value-led recovery: SSSG of just 1.5% on mid-single-digit guest counts, no price increase taken in four to five months, and gross margin guided down to ~67% from 68.1% on cocoa, coffee and geopolitical supplier inflation. Restaurant operating margin improved ~100 bps for FY26, but operating EBITDA was explicitly stable at 13.2%, so earnings power is holding rather than inflecting.
verdict.quote: Our operating EBITDA remains broadly stable year-on-year despite higher advertising and promotion spend and continued growth investments.

verdict.theme: Aerospace and defence superalloys, titanium
verdict.rationale: MIDHANI makes titanium, superalloys and maraging steel for ISRO launch vehicles, missiles, aero engines and AMCA, with 79% of the order book from defence and new NADCAP and CEMILAC airworthiness certifications opening direct OEM supply. Management reported record Q4 turnover up 34.63% with PBT up 38.67%, a Rs 2,290 crore order book, and guided to 15-20% revenue growth with 23-25% EBITDA margins.
verdict.quote: we have achieved the highest ever quarterly turnover of INR552.7 crores, registering a growth of 34.63%

verdict.theme: Retail broking and diversified capital-market services
verdict.rationale: Share India is a conventional broker and prop trader adding wealth, PMS, NBFC and merchant banking lines; its algo platform, Silverleaf HFT acquisition and 'input of AI and automation' are technology applied to its own broking back end, not a forward-looking industry. Earnings power is rising on management's own numbers: consolidated revenue up 31% and PAT up 48% year-on-year, MTF book at Rs. 470 crore heading to Rs. 1,000 crore, improved realisation, and guidance for about 20% growth this year.
verdict.quote: we remain confident of delivering around 20% growth during the current financial year

verdict.theme: Mining consumables: mill liners, grinding media
verdict.rationale: Tega supplies mill liners, grinding media and mineral-processing equipment to gold and copper mines, a conventional industrials business rather than a forward-looking industry, and the Molycop acquisition deepens that same grinding-media exposure instead of pivoting. Management reports FY26 revenue up only 5% with consumables flat, blended EBITDA margin easing from 23% to 22%, and guidance held at 21-22%, with commodity cost inflation passed on to customers at a quarter's lag; the order book is up 18% but Molycop is guided to just 3% growth on 12% margins.
verdict.quote: We have maintained healthy gross margin of 60% at the group level vis-a-vis 58% last year same period

verdict.theme: GLP-1 drug-device and biologics CDMO
verdict.rationale: Management describes a GLP-1 (semaglutide/tirzepatide) drug-device and biosimilar-biologics CDMO franchise where capacity, not demand, is the constraint, with customers paying upfront fees and take-or-pay capacity reservations. Q1 FY27 revenue grew 37% and EBITDA 39% year-on-year with mix-driven margin gains, and the FY28 guidance of $400 million organic revenue at 40% EBITDA margin was reiterated.
verdict.quote: EBITDA has also come in at INR1,233 million, which has been up significantly, 39% year-on-year

verdict.theme: Cinema exhibition and out-of-home entertainment
verdict.rationale: Management reports Q1 FY27 EBITDA nearly doubling to INR230 crores at a 14% margin on operating leverage and cost discipline, with ATP up 8%, SPH up 9%, falling F&B COGS and a net cash balance sheet. But the business is multiplex exhibition plus food courts and live screenings, not a forward-looking industry; AI-assisted dynamic pricing and app monetisation worth INR2-3 crores annually are back-office digitisation, not a pivot.
verdict.quote: EBITDA nearly doubled to INR230 crores at a 14% margin. This margin expansion reflects the benefit of operating leverage and the cost discipline we have sustained for several years.

verdict.theme: Branded textiles and apparel retail
verdict.rationale: Raymond Lifestyle is a century-old suiting, shirting and apparel business whose growth levers are premiumisation, casualisation and store economics, with digitisation limited to SAP S/4HANA and AI-assisted design, so it is not a forward-looking industry. Management reports FY26 EBITDA up 23% to INR804 crores with Q4 EBITDA up 53%, garmenting margins turning positive at 4.1%, and order books described as full into the next year.
verdict.quote: my first quarter order books are completely full

verdict.theme: Stainless steel manufacturing
verdict.rationale: Management guides EBITDA per ton of INR18,000-20,000 for H1 FY27, below the current run rate, saying fuel and utility costs rose 2.5x-3x and cannot be fully passed on because importers face no such increase. Volumes still grow 7-9% with capacity heading to 3.5 million tons by FY29, so aggregate profit holds up while per-ton margins do not expand; QCO suspension adds import pressure.
verdict.quote: the cost has gone up, and everything we are not able to pass on to our customers

verdict.theme: Indian branded formulations pharma, nascent biosimilars
verdict.rationale: Core business is conventional domestic branded generics sold by a 3,100-strong medical-rep force, with growth from added reps, price hikes on a 92% non-NLEM portfolio and acquired brands (Bayer IVF portfolio, Wokadine), so the biosimilar and semaglutide launches are portfolio additions rather than a pivot into a forward-looking industry. Earnings power is clearly rising: FY26 revenue +17.3% and adjusted PAT +33.4%, EBITDA margin up 80bps to 20.9%, gross margin 81.4% guided to hold near 80%, PCPM up from INR 3.62 lakh to INR 4.11 lakh, with FY27 guidance of 15% organic revenue growth, 25% on acquired brands and 20%+ PAT growth.
verdict.quote: Our revenue for FY26 grew at 17% while PAT increased by 33% on a year-on-year basis.

verdict.theme: Branded hotel ownership and operation, India
verdict.rationale: Management guides 9-11% same-store revenue growth with ~38% reported margins (40%+ ex-GST), 55%+ incremental flow-through, interest cost falling to ~INR 135 crores on a 7.9% rate, and free cash compounding from INR 300 crores in FY26 to over INR 3,000 crores cumulative by FY31. The business is conventional hospitality with a new-hotel pipeline, not a forward-looking industry.
verdict.quote: structurally, the company will secure its place at 40%-plus reported margins

verdict.theme: Digital payments and commerce infrastructure platform
verdict.rationale: Management guides FY2027 revenue growth of 21-23.5% after lifting EBITDA margin roughly 500 basis points in FY2026, with contribution margin held near 75% and the CFO stating there is no margin pressure and even some pricing increases. Order-book visibility is strong: nine-month advance visibility on bank and retailer infrastructure contracts, a Rs.60-65 Crore five-year Indian Oil loyalty mandate, and OMC terminals at only 50% of steady-state volumes.
verdict.quote: we are seeing no margin pressure. In fact, we are actually seeing some price ups happening in some of our segments

verdict.theme: Industrial gases; steel-led with solar specialty optionality
verdict.rationale: Ellenbarrie is a decades-old air-separation business whose volumes track steel, metals, chemicals and healthcare; management says core focus stays on oxygen, nitrogen and argon, with solar specialty gases only an add-on (a couple of solar contracts signed, no semiconductor customers yet, specialty unit only in FY28). Earnings power is improving: FY26 gases segment EBITDA margin of 38.4% was up 500bps year-on-year, argon pricing has recovered from Q3 lows, new lower-power-cost capacity is ramping, and management guides to a 40% margin and roughly 20% revenue CAGR.
verdict.quote: our core focus would continue to be on the basic air gases which are oxygen, nitrogen, argon

verdict.theme: Solar pumps, solar modules, rooftop solar, EV motors
verdict.rationale: Management confirms EBITDA fell from INR144 crores to INR83 crores year-on-year with margins down from ~24% to ~10%, blaming a 6% raw-material hit and 4% lower realization, and declined to give any margin or EBITDA guidance; the order book also shrank from INR1,500 crores to INR1,000 crores even as revenue hit a record INR859 crores. Improvement is only hoped for, contingent on geopolitics easing and the 0.5 GW module plant starting.
verdict.quote: the decline in EBITDA from INR144 crores to INR83 crores can largely be explained by these two factors

verdict.theme: Mattresses and polyurethane foam manufacturing
verdict.rationale: Sheela Foam remains a conventional mattress and foam maker; its Staqo IT unit and Furlenco furniture-rental stake are adjacent services, not a pivot into a forward-looking industry. Management reports record FY26 foam output, top line and EBITDA, consolidated core EBITDA margin up 261bps to 10.8%, PAT up 78%, successful raw-material pass-through and the first dividend since listing.
verdict.quote: the company achieved several milestones in FY '26, including highest ever annual foam production, highest ever top line and the highest ever EBITDA

verdict.theme: Digital platform for truckers, logistics tech
verdict.rationale: Management reports FY26 total income up 55% and EBITDA up 84% to ~Rs 190 crore with first full-year PAT of Rs 160 crore, and says operating leverage in the core businesses 'continues to be supremely high' with mature superloads cohorts at 30-40% EBITDA. Margin softening from ~36% to ~31% is attributed to deliberate investment in growth businesses, not pricing or demand, though management flags short-term drag from the West Asia conflict and a suspended oil-marketing loyalty programme.
verdict.quote: On a EBITDA basis we have done close to 190 crores which is a 84% growth on a year-on-year basis.

verdict.theme: Peptide/GLP-1 CDMO and complex generics
verdict.rationale: Core business is conventional generic APIs and formulations, but management is explicitly pivoting into peptide CDMO via Senn Chemicals plus Zurich and Vizag peptide capacity, with GLP-1, peptide drug conjugates and oligonucleotide optionality, and a stated target of $50 million peptide revenue at 30%-plus EBITDA within about three years. Earnings power is rising: Q1 FY27 revenue up 22%, EBITDA up 37% with margin expansion of 256 basis points, gross margin up 74 basis points on mix, ROCE at 18% and effectively debt free.
verdict.quote: Gross margin was healthy at 65.6% and expansion of 74 basis points year-on-year, led by complex generic and higher value formulations enriched our product mix

verdict.theme: Dairy and value-added dairy products
verdict.rationale: Management reports EBITDA margin of 4.6% against a 7%-7.5% historical median, with gross margin down ~2.5% on raw milk, skimmed milk powder and packing costs, and milk EBITDA falling from 5.8% to 3.03% year-on-year. Value-added products grew 40% and price hikes are ongoing, but the CEO says margin recovery depends primarily on raw milk prices coming down, which they cannot forecast.
verdict.quote: our objective is not a 6% EBITDA... we are aiming for high single-digit EBITDA... But primarily raw milk coming down will be a significant driver

verdict.theme: Generic pharmaceuticals and branded exports
verdict.rationale: Strides is a conventional generics and branded formulations maker; its growth drivers are nasal sprays, controlled substances, Africa brands and an Africa portfolio bought from Sandoz, not a forward-looking industry. Management reports EBITDA margin expansion of 400 basis points to 19% over three years, operational PAT up 50% year-on-year, gross margins held at 58-60% despite price erosion, and guides to EBITDA above 20%, so earnings power is clearly improving even with Q4 freight cost pressure.
verdict.quote: EBITDA compounded at approximately 26% over the last 3 years, driven by the EBITDA margin expansion of 400 basis points to close FY26 at 19%

verdict.theme: Seamless steel pipes for oil and gas
verdict.rationale: Core business is seamless and ERW pipe for ONGC/Oil India drilling, a conventional cyclical steel-tube business with a small 59.5 MW captive renewable vertical and no pivot; management explicitly said 'we don't want to diversify'. Earnings power is flat rather than rising: the Q3 margin uptick was only the reversal of a notional inventory markdown, dispatches were flat (103,000 then 101,000 tons), Chinese imports still run 20-25% of domestic production, project awards fell 27% year-on-year, capex is being delayed, and guidance is INR10,000-15,000 per ton with no order-book visibility beyond three to four months.
verdict.quote: we don't see margins to decline materially from here. I think it will remain in the range of INR10,000 to INR15,000 per ton.

verdict.theme: Consumer wellness, nutrition and personal-care brands
verdict.rationale: Management frames the business as FMCG wellness brands (Glucon-D, Nycil, Complan, Everyuth, Sugar Free, RiteBite) plus the Comfort Click online vitamins business, so the digital element is a sales channel rather than a forward-looking industry. On earnings, Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 42.2% and full-year 34.2%, gross margins were described as in line or better with per-brand margin gains, and Comfort Click turned EPS accretive with operating leverage still to come, despite weak seasonal brands dragging PAT via amortisation.
verdict.quote: Each of the brands within our domestic range has increased our margins

verdict.theme: Road/infra EPC, coal MDO, InvIT road assets
verdict.rationale: Core business is conventional highway EPC plus coal mine developer-operator work and road InvIT assets; the solar and transmission SPVs are build-and-sell EPC mandates where DBL funds only 15% of equity and is already hunting an acquirer, not a pivot into renewables. Management guides FY27 revenue up 30-40% on a record INR28,000 crore order book at a maintained 11-12% EBITDA margin, with mining revenue scaling from INR1,600 crore to about INR4,000 crore by FY29, though crude-linked bitumen and HSD costs are only partly passed through and FY26 profit after tax was flattered by InvIT transfer gains.
verdict.quote: we are confident that as scale hits and as we also complete our coal-handling plant and hit COD, the margins will meaningfully improve

verdict.theme: Process equipment pivoting to semiconductors, nuclear, defence
verdict.rationale: Core glass-lined reactor business for chemicals/pharma is conventional, but management says nearly half of FY26 order intake now comes from non-traditional segments — semiconductors (Edlon linings for Micron/Intel, grown from USD 10mn to USD 25mn, 'high margin business, and good growth'), a INR 130 crore nuclear order, defence, and lithium extraction/battery systems. Earnings power is improving off a low base: FY26 revenue +10%, EBITDA +11% with margin up ~1pp, order intake +20% to INR 3,714 crore, opening backlog +34%, plus a quantified INR 45 crore annual saving from the German restructuring and a stated 15% EBITDA target versus 11.4% today, though management repeatedly cautions the gain will be gradual.
verdict.quote: Nearly 50% of our order intake this year has come from non-traditional industries.

verdict.theme: Steel, ferro alloys, coal mining, power generation
verdict.rationale: Core business is secondary steel, ferro alloys, captive coal mines and 600MW thermal IPP — conventional commodity/utility, with hydro and a 50MW captive solar plant as adjuncts rather than a pivot into a forward-looking industry. Earnings power is improving: Q3 EBITDA rose to INR395cr from INR368cr YoY and 9M PAT was up 59%, with management citing a 12-15% blended steel price recovery from Q3 lows, IPP tariffs moving above INR5/unit, 200MW medium-term plus 100MW long-term PPAs signed and a 40-year Rehar hydro PPA at INR7.42/unit.
verdict.quote: We remain confident of delivering record results for financial year '26 despite sectoral challenges in the steel sector.

verdict.theme: Pharma CRDMO: biotech discovery, peptides, ADCs
verdict.rationale: FY26 revenue +29%, EBITDA +56% and PAT +109% with EBITDA already at 30% against a 28-30% aspiration, 34 commercial molecules plus 11 in Phase III/pre-registration, and FY27 capex stepped up to INR1,100-1,300 crores on stated demand visibility; management flags input-cost and logistics inflation and scale-up inefficiency as margin offsets but keeps 15-20% growth guidance and expects H2 FY27 stronger than H1.
verdict.quote: delivered a strong performance in FY26 with overall revenue growth of 29%, EBITDA growth of 56%, and PAT growth of 109%
